syllabus_topics: Mathematics for Computer Graphics (includes trigonometry and matrices)
Geometric Transformations: Elementary planar geometric transformations
Clipping (Cohen-Sutherland and Sutherland-Hodgman) and hidden surface removal
Fragment operations: buffer memories and texture mapping
New hardware/software architectures in Computer Graphics

assessment_methods.method: Theoretical (best five out of six MAP10)

assessment_rules: For continuous assessment, a minimum of 40% (8 marks) is required in both Laboratories and Theoretical components to pass. The final grade in the "normal period" is 100% continuous assessment. For the "resource period", the final grade is 50% theoretical component (better of 5/6 MAP10 or resource exam) + 50% laboratories. For working students, the theoretical component is the better of 5/6 MAP10 or resource exam (50%) and laboratories (50%). For the "special period", the assessment is 50% exam and 50% laboratories (or equivalent project). Students with grades above 17 may be required to take a special supplementary exam; failure or non-attendance will result in a grade of 17.
